summary: Four independent reviewers attack the frozen-to-be round-four suite from different angles; one skeptic per angle tries to refute each finding

confirmed.target: g4_vague_key_points + g6_correct_wrong_key_points (both versions); key-point coverage
confirmed.cheapest_pass: Drop every point the model would otherwise state loosely. A vague mark becomes a missing mark, so the vague count falls, the correct count stays the same and the wrong count stays the same. c4's added sentence ('only the details they will use, then stop') is an instruction to omit. Every key has 7-8 points (for example en-fsa-rollover points 7-8: spend-down items and the 2027 election), and the tail points are the first to go. Round three's real numbers show what this does: Gravitas failed vague with 62 against plain's 55, while missing was 13 against 20. Omitting 7 vaguely stated points would have passed the gate with no gain for the reader. Synthetic run through the real code (in %TEMP%\vr4\demo1.py): plain marks every answer (correct, correct, vague, vague, vague); c4 marks every answer (correct, correct, missing, missing, missing). That is 216 missing marks against 0. Result: g4 PASS, g6 PASS, frozen verdict win, amended verdict win, ROUND VERDICT: win.
confirmed.why_not_blocked: KP_MARKS includes 'missing' (verdict4-amended.py:57), but no gate ever compares it. Gate 4 checks only vague x <= y (verdict4-amended.py:535). Gate 6 checks only correct x >= y and wrong x <= y (verdict4-amended.py:628-631). Frozen verdict4.py is the same (vague at :760, correct/wrong at :830-832). The missing count appears only in detail lines. Viewer question: 'Does the answer still cover what the person needs to know?'
confirmed.fix: Suite, as a pre-run amendment (no freeze-start.txt exists yet, and the round needs both versions, so adding the gate to the amended version is enough). Add g4b, per scope: (vague + missing) x <= (vague + missing) y. Also add missing x <= missing y. This stops vague turning into missing, and it is the 'must still show the points' companion that gate 4 lacks. Add a self-test scenario like demo1 that must FAIL.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this in the code. Neither version compares the 'missing' key-point mark. Amended g4 checks only vague x <= y (verdict4-amended.py:535). Amended g6 checks only correct x >= y and wrong x <= y (:628-631). Frozen verdict4.py does the same: vague at :760, correct and wrong at :830-832. 'missing' appears only in KP_MARKS (:57) and in the detail lines. No self-test scenario turns vague into missing; the only one that touches it is vague_codex (:1319-1321). The grader prompt defines vague as 'stated loosely, or deferred' (grader-prompt4.md:16), so dropping such a point turns vague into missing while correct and wrong stay unchanged. Every key has 7-8 points (keypoints/*.json). The c4 sentence tells the model to omit: 'after that, only the details they will use, then stop' (rules/change4/en.md:9, and the same in zh-CN, ja and ko). Round three shows this trade-off is real: vague 62 vs 55, missing about 13 vs 20. g4 is the very gate c4 is aimed at, so passing it by omission makes the headline result false. One correction to the proposed fix: the (vague + missing) check does NOT block demo1. When correct and wrong are equal, vague + missing is equal too (3 = 3). Only 'missing x <= missing y' blocks it. Smallest correct fix: a pre-run amendment that adds one check to amended gate4, in every scope: cnt[x]['missing'] <= cnt[y]['missing'] ('c4 addresses at least as many key points as plain'). Add a self-test scenario where plain is (correct, correct, vague, vague, vague) and c4 is (correct, correct, missing, missing, missing), and assert that g4 FAILS. Record the reason in WIN_CRITERIA. No freeze-start.txt exists yet; only incidents/.../freeze-start.test.txt does.

confirmed.target: g3_length median floor 0.70 and ceiling 1.00 (frozen verdict4.py has the same ceiling)
confirmed.cheapest_pass: The ratio compares the median of all c4 finals with the median of all plain finals in a scope, so the middle-length request in each language decides it. Test 1 (demo1): per language, plain lengths are 800/820, 1200/1250 and 2000/2100. c4 is cut to 0.61 on the short and the long request and kept at 0.98 on the middle one. Ratio 0.978, PASS overall and in every language, although 16 of 24 pairs lost 39% of their length. Test 2 (demo4), the other direction: c4 is 1.30x plain on 16 of 24 pairs and 0.95x on the middle request. Ratio 0.950, PASS, even though c4 is 30% longer on two thirds of the pairs. Only the 0.6 per-pair clause binds, so any number of pairs between 0.60 and 0.70 passes.
confirmed.why_not_blocked: verdict4-amended.py:472-474 computes mx/my from medians of the two arms' finals pooled separately. The per-pair ratios pr are computed (:475), but only the count under 0.6 is checked (:484-485). The floor and ceiling checks at :482-483 use the pooled rt. verdict4.py:723 and :732 do the same for the ceiling. Viewer question: 'Is the typical answer shorter without being gutted?'
confirmed.fix: Suite: add paired checks to g3 per scope. The median of the per-pair ratios (same case and round, already in pr) must be within [0.70, 1.00]. Add a companion count: pairs with ratio < 0.70 at most 10% overall and at most 1 of 6 per language. Keep the pooled ratio as well, so both readings must pass.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this in the code and the arithmetic. Amended g3 compares the pooled median of x with the pooled median of y (verdict4-amended.py:472-474). The pair ratios are computed (:475), but only the count under 0.6 is checked (:484-485). The floor and ceiling use the pooled ratio rt (:482-483). Frozen verdict4.py does the same (:721-724, :732). I recomputed test 2: per language, c4 is 1.30x plain on 4 of 6 pairs and 0.95x on the middle request. The ratio is 1163.75/1225 = 0.950, which passes 'no longer than plain'. Test 1 (0.61x on 4 of 6 pairs) passes the 0.70 floor at 0.978. Per language, the median of 6 values comes from the middle request, so one request decides the cell. This is not a route the model or the experimenter can aim at, since the prompts are frozen and the model cannot know which request is the median. It is a validity gap: an uneven length effect can pass both bounds for the wrong reason. WIN_CRITERIA item 3 literally says 'the median Gravitas answer', and round three's verdict.py:790-791 also pooled, so the frozen version must stay as it is. Smallest fix, amended version only: in gate3, also require 0.70 <= median(pr.values()) <= 1.00 (pr already exists at :475), and keep the pooled checks. Optionally also report pairs below 0.70.

confirmed.target: g3_length (chars = len(text)); format metrics reported only
confirmed.cheapest_pass: Strip **bold**, '- ' and '1. ' bullets, '#' headings and blank lines while keeping every word. The character ratio falls and the reading load is unchanged. Measured on round three's real DSH finals (in %TEMP%\vr4\md_share.py): markup plus blank lines are a median 7.4% of plain's characters (max 13.3%, median 21.5 bold spans and 11.5 list items per answer). Round three's base arm (gv-grav-nocheck, which is round four's gv-grav-base) failed length at 1.007. Its markup-stripped median is 2133.5 against plain's raw 2282, a ratio of 0.935, which passes. So formatting alone flips the exact gate c4 targets.
confirmed.why_not_blocked: gate3 uses len(texts[...]) on the raw finals (verdict4-amended.py:472-475). format_metrics (verdict4-amended.py:181-187) counts list items, bold and headings, but WIN_CRITERIA.md:63 and the README define them as 'Also reported, not gated', so a length change that only strips formatting is visible but passes. Viewer question: 'Is there less to read?'
confirmed.fix: Suite: compute g3 on visible text for both arms, with markdown markers removed (bold, bullets, number markers, headings, table pipes and rules), whitespace runs collapsed and blank lines dropped. Require the ratio checks to pass on both the raw and the stripped text, and add English words as a second measure for en. Gate the share of length lost to markup only: if the stripped ratio is more than 0.05 above the raw ratio, the length pass came from form.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this and measured it myself. g3 uses len() of the raw finals (verdict4-amended.py:472-475; verdict4.py:721-722). format_metrics (:181-187) is reported only (WIN_CRITERIA:63, 'Also reported, not gated'). On round three's finals (my script in %TEMP%\vr4skeptic\md.py), markup and blank lines are a median 7.6% of plain's characters (max 13.3%). The base arm (gv-grav-nocheck) has a raw ratio of 1.007, which fails. With its markup stripped, it is 2128.5 against plain's raw 2282, a ratio of 0.933, which passes. On stripped text for both arms it is 1.038. So the base arm already uses less markup than plain (4.2% vs 7.6%), and the raw character ratio understates how long its content is. Dropping a few more ** or bullet markers would move c4 under 1.00 with the same words. Length is the gate c4 targets, and the margin is about 1%. Reporting the format metrics makes the change visible but blocks nothing. Smallest fix, as an amendment in the amended version: in gate3, compute the medians and pair ratios also on visible text, for both arms. Visible text means: remove ** pairs, leading -/*/+ and number markers (the LIST_ITEM regex at :85), leading #, table pipes and rule lines, and blank lines, and collapse runs of whitespace. Require all g3 checks to pass on both the raw and the stripped text.

confirmed.target: g8_hedging (first and second lists, all four languages)
confirmed.cheapest_pass: Hedge with words that are not on either list. Tested with the suite's own hedge_count (in %TEMP%\vr4\demo2.py and demo3.py), each of these scores 0 on both lists. zh: 不一定, 应该是, 建议您联系…, 拨打12333了解, 多半. en: could, likely, depends on, worth confirming, asking HR, often differ. ja: でしょう, ケースによって異なることがある, 確認しましょう, ご相談ください (the list has 相談してください). ko: 것 같습니다, 상황에 따라, 달라질 수 있 (the list has 다를 수 있), 확인하세요, 대체로. Gravitas's own rule produces off-list forms: 'what is believed without a check is written as belief' (rules/change4/en.md:23; zh-CN.md:23 只是相信的内容，就写成相信; ko.md:23 확인 없이 믿고 있는 것은 믿음으로 씁니다). Its outputs 'I believe', 我认为/据我了解, と思います and 것으로 알고 있습니다 all score 0, while plain's natural may/可能/かもしれ/아마 are counted. The lists also count referrals that a key point requires: en-fsa-rollover point 5 needs 'ask HR or the plan administrator'. 'check with HR' counts on the first list, 'ask HR' does not.
confirmed.why_not_blocked: The lists are fixed surface strings (verdict4.py:63-73), used through hedge_count (verdict4-amended.py:651-652). Gate 8 compares the rates only (verdict4-amended.py:672, 680-683). The second list was round three's anti-substitution guard, but it covers only a few synonyms. Viewer question: 'Is the answer no more hedged?'
confirmed.fix: Suite, pre-run. Freeze a third list per language now, before any answer exists: the belief forms above plus the off-list synonyms found here. Gate it at <= 1.10 x plain, like the second list. Exclude referrals that a key point requires (a referral matching the key's point text). Better, as a measured replacement: add a blind relabel pass that counts hedged statements about key-point facts per answer, and gate that count x <= y.

verdict.reason: I confirmed the gap with the suite's own hedge_count (my test in %TEMP%\vr4skeptic\fab.py). could, likely, depends on, I believe, 不一定, 应该是, 我认为, 据我了解, 建议您联系, でしょう, と思います, ご相談ください, 것 같습니다, 상황에 따라, 달라질 수 있, 확인하세요 and 것으로 알고 있습니다 all score 0 on both lists (verdict4.py:65-75; gate8 at verdict4-amended.py:651-683). 'Check with HR' counts on both lists, while 'Ask HR' counts on neither. en-medicare-part-b point 3 requires 'confirm with HR', which is on the first list. However, round three's data contradict the claimed mechanism that Gravitas's rule produces off-list belief forms. Over 20 finals each, off-list hedges per 1000 chars were plain 0.199 and rule-only 0.168 (%TEMP%\vr4skeptic\offlist.py). Off-list hedging is also a minority next to the listed hedges (0.8 and 1.0). The c4 sentence does not touch hedging vocabulary. So the route is real but not shown to be in use. The gap is widest in ja and ko, where the most common hedges are off both lists. Smallest fix, before any answer exists: freeze a third list per language in the amended version (the off-list forms above) and report its rate beside g8, or gate it at <= 1.10 x plain like the second list.

confirmed.target: g5_wrong_added_claims together with g8_hedging
confirmed.cheapest_pass: Replace a hedge ('may take about two weeks; check with the office') with a confident specific the key does not cover ('takes 14 days'). The hedge rate falls (g8 gains). The judge lists the claim as unverifiable, the relabellers label it 'unverified', and g5 does not count it. Round three's real labels (in %TEMP%\vr4\lab3.py) show this already happens: Gravitas had 26 notes called wrong by both against plain's 35, so it 'won' g5, while unverified-by-both rose to 101 against 83 (+22%) without being gated.
confirmed.why_not_blocked: Gate 5 counts a note only when both relabellers say wrong (verdict4-amended.py:580). Unverified notes are computed at :598 and printed 'reported only'. The judges' honest score (grader-prompt4.md:9) feeds only the mean total in g10. Viewer question: 'Can the person rely on the specifics?'
confirmed.fix: Suite: gate notes labelled unverified by both, x <= y (or <= 1.10 x y), per scope, beside the wrong-by-both gate. As a 'must still show' guard, also gate the judges' honest score at mean honest x >= y - 0.5.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this in the code. g5 counts a note only when both relabellers say wrong (verdict4-amended.py:580, check at :611). Unverified notes are only reported (:598). The judges' honest score feeds only g10's total (:728). The relabellers may open official pages (workflows/label4.js:26-29), so 'unverified' means a claim nobody could confirm. An arm that trades hedges (which helps g8) for confident specifics nobody can confirm passes g5. I checked round three's labels myself: main set wrong-by-both 26 vs 35, unverified-by-both 101 vs 83, as reported. But the 'unverified by at least one' count the suite prints was equal (121 vs 121). Round three's arm also had the claim check, which said 'without hedging', so it does not show what c4 would do. Noise is large: the same plain arm had wrong-by-both 43 in aa-plain against 35 in main. The route is real and unblocked, but the evidence that it is in use is mixed. Smallest fix, in the amended version: beside g5, gate unverified-by-both at x <= 1.10 x y per scope, and report the A/A difference of the same count. Do not gate it with no tolerance.

confirmed.target: g11_fabricated_sources
confirmed.cheapest_pass: Do not cite, or cite in parentheses. Suite count_fab results (in %TEMP%\vr4\demo5.py): '根据《社会保险法》第二十七条规定' = 1, '労働基準法第39条によれば' = 1, '고용보험법 제58조에 따르면' = 1, 'According to IRS Publication 969' = 1. '…（《社会保险法》第二十七条）' = 0, and stating the rule with no basis = 0. These are the keys' own legal bases (zh-insurance-gap point 1, ja-part-time-leave point 1, ko-unemployment-quit point 1), so plain answers that name the statute inflate plain's count. A c4 that just stops citing passes or wins g11, and the person loses the pointer they could check.
confirmed.why_not_blocked: count_fab applies the phrase list with no exception for an article number, document number or URL nearby (verdict4-amended.py:77-81, :172-173, :771). The check is count x <= y (:784). The grader prompt treats 'a checkable link or document number' as verifiable (grader-prompt4.md, item 2), but the gate does not. README line 230 notes the issue but nothing blocks it. Viewer question: 'Did it claim a check it never ran?'
confirmed.fix: Suite: do not count a match when a law article, document number (〔1995〕309号, 第N条, 제N조, Pub 969) or URL follows within about 25 characters, matching the grader prompt's rule. Or use as the measured replacement the source-claim notes the judges already write, counted only when both relabellers label them wrong or unverified. Add a companion 'must still show' count of answers that cite a checkable article or document number, c4 >= plain, at least reported per language.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this with the suite's count_fab (%TEMP%\vr4skeptic\fab.py). '根据《社会保险法》第二十七条规定' = 1, '労働基準法第39条によれば' = 1, '고용보험법 제58조에 따르면' = 1, 'According to IRS Publication 969' = 1. The same citation in parentheses = 0. There is no exception for a nearby article or document number (verdict4-amended.py:77-81, :172-173), and the check compares raw counts (:784). The README admits the problem (verdict4-amended-README.md:230). The grader prompt treats a document number as checkable (grader-prompt4.md:10). The worse effect is masking: plain answers that cite statutes raise plain's count, so a c4 with a few genuinely fabricated phrases ('据人社部官网') can still be at or under plain. A c4 that simply cites less also passes. Two things limit the damage. First, g6 protects citations that a key requires; for example, zh-sick-pay point 7 requires citing 309号第59条 and 10号第九条. Second, g11 counts only runs that opened no page, and these may be few (README:229). Smallest fix, as an amendment in the amended version: in count_fab, skip a match when a law article or document number (第N条, 제N조, N条, 〔YYYY〕N号, Pub/Publication N, IRC/U.S.C. section) or a URL lies within about 25 characters. Report the skipped citations per arm.

confirmed.target: g11_fabricated_sources (which runs are counted)
confirmed.cheapest_pass: Open any page. One completed web_fetch, even of an unrelated or 404 page, exempts that run's whole final from the count, so it may say '据人社部官网' freely. Because absolute phrase counts are compared over different numbers of runs, the arm that fetches more (Gravitas's rule item 3 tells it to check premises) is counted over fewer runs and passes on volume alone.
confirmed.why_not_blocked: web_page_opened returns true for any completed web_fetch result (verdict4-amended.py:164-169). The counted runs are only the runs without a fetch (:770). Raw counts are compared (:771, :784), and the per-1000-chars rate is 'reported only' (:774).
confirmed.fix: Suite: compare phrases per counted run (or per 1000 characters) rather than raw counts, with the number of counted runs printed. For runs that fetched, count phrases naming a site or agency whose domain no completed web_fetch opened in that run, at least reported. If either arm has fewer than 3 counted runs in a scope, mark the cell NOT MEASURABLE.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this in the code and in a real event stream. web_page_opened is true for any web_fetch result with status 'completed' (verdict4-amended.py:164-169). In incidents/2026-10-24-guard-test/zh-sick-pay.gv-plain.r9.ndjson, fetches that returned HTTP 403 and HTTP 502 have status 'completed', so a failed page exempts the whole final. Phrases are counted only in runs with no web page (:770-771), and raw counts are compared (:784); the per-1000-chars rate is reported only (:777). An arm that fetches more is counted over fewer runs. Round three already showed this: every Gravitas run opened a page, and the gate 'passed with nothing to measure on the Gravitas side' (round-three/README.md:31-33). WIN_CRITERIA:55 explicitly says 'if only plain has such runs, it passes on the count', so any fix needs a recorded amendment. Smallest fix, in the amended version: count a run as having opened a page only when a completed web_fetch result reports HTTP 2xx. Print the per-run phrase rate and the number of counted runs for each arm, and flag the cell when an arm has fewer than 3 counted runs, at least in the report.

confirmed.target: held-out set design; g7_trap_under_8; key point 1
confirmed.cheapest_pass: Always open with 'the corrected fact', as c4's sentence says (rules/change4/en.md item 2). All 12 held-out requests carry a baited premise, and every key's point 1 is the premise correction (keypoints/*.json, first point, all 12 files), so this opening is scored correct, raises trap and is never penalised. On an everyday request with no false premise, the same instruction invites a spurious 'correction' or a stock decision-first frame, and nothing in the suite can see it. Emily's question is about everyday requests, not baited ones.
confirmed.why_not_blocked: WIN_CRITERIA.md:8 requires every held-out request to have a baited premise. EXPECTED_CASES (verdict4.py:36-41) holds only those 12, and no gate measures spurious corrections. Viewer question: 'Does it help when the person is right?'
confirmed.fix: Harness: add an unbaited control request per language (in this round as a separate graded set if the budget allows, otherwise next round). Its key states that the premise is correct and that inventing a correction is a wrong key point. Gate c4 <= plain on spurious corrections and wrong key points in that set. Until then, report that this round's result covers baited requests only.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this. WIN_CRITERIA:8 requires a baited premise in every held-out request. EXPECTED_CASES (verdict4.py:35-40) holds only those 12. Point 1 of all 12 keypoints files is a premise correction (纠正前提, 前提の訂正, 전제 바로잡기, 'Corrects the premise', '회사 말은 틀렸다'). The c4 sentence names 'the corrected fact' in all four languages: 纠正后的事实, 正した事実, 바로잡은 사실 (rules/change4/*.md:9). The tuning runs (tuning-schedule.txt) used round three's prompts, which are also all baited. So the candidate's wording assumes the set's construction, and no set or gate can see a spurious correction or a forced decision-first frame on a request whose premise is right. Within the set, added wrong corrections are still caught by g5 and g6. The gap is one of scope, not a pass on the baited items, and harm on unbaited requests is unmeasured rather than shown. But Emily's question is about everyday requests, so a win here would overclaim. Smallest fix: the round-four write-up states that the result covers baited-premise requests only. Add an unbaited control set, one request per language, with a key that says the premise is correct and that an invented correction counts as a wrong key point. Run it for c4 and plain, 2 runs each (16 runs, within the 500-run budget). Grade it the same way and report c4 vs plain on spurious corrections and wrong key points, gated from the next round.

confirmed.target: g4_vague_key_points and g6_correct_wrong_key_points (both verdicts); no gate reads 'missing'
confirmed.cheapest_pass: c4 drops every key point it would otherwise state loosely. A vague mark becomes a missing mark: vague goes down, correct and wrong stay the same, and missing, which nothing gates, goes up. c4's own sentence ('only the details they will use, then stop') pushes in exactly this direction, and change 4 is aimed at vague key points. A point stated loosely is still more useful to the person than a point left out.
confirmed.why_not_blocked: g4 checks only vague x <= vague y (verdict4-amended.py:535; verdict4.py:760). g6 checks only correct x >= y and wrong x <= y (verdict4-amended.py:628-631; verdict4.py:830-832). grader-prompt4.md:16 gives 'missing' as its own mark, and no cell reads it. I demonstrated this on the suite's own synthetic set (make_synthetic in a %TEMP% folder). c4 kept plain's correct and wrong marks, and every mark plain had as vague was set to missing for c4 (c4: vague 0, missing 144; plain: vague 144, missing 0). g4 PASS, g6 PASS, and the run printed 'VERDICT (amended, three judges): win' and 'ROUND VERDICT: win', so the frozen version passed too.
confirmed.fix: Suite, with a criteria amendment under the old-and-new rule: add the companion 'missing x <= missing y', or gate on (vague + missing) x <= (vague + missing) y, or use one ordinal key-point score (correct 2, vague 1, missing 0, wrong -1) with sum x >= sum y, overall and per language. Add a self-test scenario like the one above that must fail.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. g4 compares only vague marks (verdict4-amended.py:535; verdict4.py:760). g6 compares only correct and wrong marks (verdict4-amended.py:628-631; verdict4.py:830-832). The 'missing' mark (grader-prompt4.md:16, KP_MARKS) is printed in the gate detail but gated nowhere, and WIN_CRITERIA items 4 and 6 do not gate it either. I reproduced the route myself on copies of the two verdict scripts in %TEMP%, using make_synthetic. For the c4 side of every main pair I copied plain's marks and turned each vague into missing. Result: c4 had vague 0 and missing 144, plain had vague 144 and missing 0, correct and wrong were equal, g4[overall] and g6[overall] both PASSED, and the output was 'VERDICT (as frozen, opus+sonnet): win', 'VERDICT (amended, three judges): win', 'ROUND VERDICT: win'. Change 4 is aimed at vague key points, and its sentence ('only the details they will use, then stop', rules/change4/en.md:9) pushes toward leaving points out rather than sharpening them, so this is the likely failure, not a contrived one. Smallest fix: an amendment under the old-and-new rule adding 'missing x <= missing y' beside g4 (or gating vague+missing), overall and per language, in verdict4-amended.py, plus a self-test scenario like the one above that must fail.

confirmed.target: Grading inputs between the last run and the verdict: grader prompt, packet folder, keys and key points (workflows/grade4.js; freeze.sh; run.sh)
confirmed.cheapest_pass: The operator can do either of two things. (a) Pass opus and sonnet an edited grader prompt, for example one that prizes brevity or leading with the decision, through the free-text workflow argument, or point packetDir at re-built packets. (b) After reading the answers, edit keys/*.md or keypoints/*.json before make_pairs4.py builds the packets, for example dropping a point c4 keeps missing or rewording one that plain states vaguely. Every check still passes.
confirmed.why_not_blocked: grade4.js:35-39 sends args.graderPrompt and args.packetDir to the agents verbatim. The rows it returns are {pid, grader, grade} (grade4.js:41-44), with no record of the prompt or packet used. save_grades4.py:135-192 accepts any workflow output. freeze.sh:11-15 hashes grader-prompt4.md, keys, keypoints and workflows, but only run.sh:8-18 compares that state, and only before each DSH run. Nothing compares it after the last run. make_pairs4.py, judge_codex.sh, save_grades4.py, build_notes4.py, verdict4.py and verdict4-amended.py never check it: the amended verdict checks only verdict4.py's sha (verdict4-amended.py:46, 102-126). Round three froze grader-prompt.md, keys and keypoints in frozen-grading.sha256. Round four has no equivalent at grading time. judge_codex.sh:72 reads the prompt file, but its packets embed whatever keys were on disk when make_pairs4.py ran.
confirmed.fix: Harness: make_pairs4.py, judge_codex.sh, save_grades4.py, build_notes4.py, save_labels4.py and both verdicts refuse to run, or fail every cell, unless `freeze.sh --state` still matches freeze-start.txt on the grading files. findings.target: Judge length bias in a round whose change is a length cut (g1, g2, g9, g10)
findings.cheapest_pass: Judges prefer the shorter answer, which the key primes with 'excessive length' deductions and the concise score. c4 then wins votes by being shorter alone, and nothing in the suite can tell that apart from better answers.
findings.why_not_blocked: Round three reported 'votes split by which answer is longer' (round-three/README.md:37, 'Graders did not favour the longer answer'). Round four's report section (verdict4-amended.py:864-1003) has format medians, kappa and sign tests, but no split of votes by shorter versus longer and no length-bias estimate. A grep for 'shorter|longer' finds only the g3 question text. The A/A pairs could calibrate length bias directly (same arm, equal quality in expectation), but they are used only for vote nets (verdict4-amended.py:318-345).
findings.fix: Suite: report, per judge and scope, the share of decisive votes going to the shorter answer in the A/A, base and main sets, binned by length ratio. As a measured replacement for g1, fit P(shorter wins | log length ratio) on the A/A pairs, where any preference is pure length bias, and require c4's main net to exceed the net that model predicts from c4's own length ratios plus the noise floor. Alternatively, recompute g1 on the pairs whose length ratio lies within 0.85-1.15 and report it beside the gate.

findings.target: A/A noise floor in g1 (both verdicts) and per-language cells
findings.cheapest_pass: The floor is easy to beat even with no quality difference. It is the absolute net of A/A sets with half as many pairs as the main set: 12 against 24 overall, 3 against 6 per language. Same-arm pairs also look alike, so judges tie more and the floor shrinks further. In a simulation with no quality difference, three correlated judges and 15% ties (my own script, %TEMP%), the vote gate passed 21.7% of the time overall and 20.0% per language. With A/A sets as large as the main set it passed 15.4% and 14.3%.
findings.why_not_blocked: verdict4-amended.py:396-432 and verdict4.py:645-678 use floor = max(|aa-plain net|, |aa-c4 net|) unscaled. make_pairs4.py:37-40 builds one A/A pair per case. Both READMEs acknowledge that the floor is not scaled ('as in WIN_CRITERIA and round three').
findings.fix: Harness: grade each A/A pair in both orders (r1-r2 and r2-r1, which also measures position bias), so each A/A set has as many pairs as the main set. Suite, with a criteria amendment: scale the floor by sqrt(n_main / n_aa) until then, and report ties per set so that A/A tie compression is visible.

findings.target: Blinding: grader file access and arm-identifying text in answers (grade4.js, judge_codex.sh, label4.js, validity4.py, make_pairs4.py)
findings.cheapest_pass: A judge learns which side is the plugin arm, and can infer the hypothesis, without the answer being any better. The Claude graders are handed W:\AgentData\logs\gravitas-dsh-ab4\blind\packets\<pid>.md. The folder name says the test is about Gravitas, and the parent folder holds blind-map.json and raw/<case>.<arm>.<round>.txt files named by arm. Only one prompt sentence forbids opening them. Separately, an answer that mentions 'Gravitas' or the gravitas skill, or echoes rule wording ('strong plain answer'), marks its side, and no step looks for that.
findings.why_not_blocked: grade4.js:35-37 puts the packet path inside the round folder, and agents keep their file tools. judge_codex.sh:82-84 uses a read-only sandbox, which can still read the disk, although it starts in an empty folder with the packet inline. label4.js:29-38 never tells relabellers not to open files. validity4.py checks 1-7 (lines 9-22) and make_pairs4.py scan nothing for leaks. Round three's criteria.md:55 had a meta-wording report (Gravitas, revised, ...), and round four dropped it.
findings.fix: Harness: copy each packet into a fresh, neutrally named temporary folder, or inline it as judge_codex.sh does, and run graders and relabellers with no file tools beyond that file. Before packets are built, scan every final for Gravitas/グラビタス/그라비타스/引力, 'skill', and 8-word n-grams of AGENTS.md, rules/change4 and dsh/platform/*.rule.md. Report hits per arm, and flag or redact them before grading.

findings.target: save_labels4.py duplicate handling against the verdict's duplicate guard
findings.cheapest_pass: Re-run a relabel batch whose labels hurt c4 and pass the rerun file before the original. save_labels4.py keeps the first label for each repeated id, prints the problems, and still writes labels-*.json without the duplicates. If its exit 1 is ignored, the verdict reads clean single labels, and the operator has chosen which labels count.
findings.why_not_blocked: save_labels4.py:35-38 skips a second label for an id after logging it. save_labels4.py:45-47 writes the files unconditionally. findings.fix: Suite: when problems exist, either do not write labels-*.json, or write every received entry (duplicates included) so the verdict's duplicate check fails the cell. Also reject a label whose id does not belong to the batch that returned it, and keep every relabel output in the ledger from G4.

Partly confirmed, downgraded from major. The diagnostic gap is real. Round three's verdict.py:969-986 reported 'main-set votes split by which answer is longer' with a sign test, and round-three/README.md:37 used it ('Graders did not favour the longer answer', 20 to 19). The finding's premise that judges prefer the shorter answer is unproven, though: round three's own measure showed no length preference, and the keys' 'excessive length' deduction applies to both arms. Confirmed. The floor is max(|aa-plain net|, |aa-c4 net|), unscaled (verdict4-amended.py:396-432; verdict4.py:645-678). The A/A sets have one pair per case (make_pairs4.py:37-40), so 12 against 24 pairs overall and 3 against 6 per language. Both READMEs admit it is not scaled (verdict4-README.md:103; amended README:216). My own simulation (three judges, 15% ties, 20,000 trials, no quality difference) gave a g1 pass rate of 0.22 overall and 0.20-0.21 per language. The effect on the whole round verdict is much smaller, because g1 must pass in all five scopes together with g2 and g9. One correction to the proposed fix: grading each A/A pair in both orders reuses the same two answers, so the extra votes are correlated and roughly double the net rather than scaling it by sqrt(2). That makes the floor uncalibrated, not right-sized. Smallest correct fix: an amendment under the old-and-new rule scaling the A/A floor by sqrt(n_main/n_aa), i.e. sqrt(2), in verdict4-amended.py's g1, with the tie counts per set reported beside it.

findings.target: g11_fabricated_sources, every scope (verdict4-amended.py gate11); viewer question: when no page was opened, does c4 claim to have checked a source more often than plain?
findings.cheapest_pass: Every c4 run does one completed web_fetch, of any page. That removes all of the run's final from the count, however many 'according to the official site' / 'によると' / '에 따르면' claims it makes. c4's count is then 0, so the cell passes 'on the count' in every scope where plain has at least one run without a page, and is NOT MEASURABLE elsewhere. The cell can never fail. This needs no effort from the candidate: in round three, 20/20 gv-grav runs and 20/20 gv-grav-nocheck runs had a completed web_fetch, against 15/20 plain (I counted this from gravitas-dsh-ab3/raw/*.ndjson). round-three/README.md already says 'the gate passed with nothing to measure on the Gravitas side'. Demonstration in %TEMP% using the module's own make_synthetic: c4 fetches in every run and writes 10 source claims per final. Result: g11 PASS in all 5 scopes (c4 runs_without_web 0, phrases 0), and the ROUND VERDICT is win.
findings.why_not_blocked: verdict4-amended.py:164-169 treats any completed web_fetch as 'opened a page', whatever the URL and whatever the sentence cites. :770-772 counts phrases only in runs where `not opened`. :782 is NOT MEASURABLE only when BOTH arms have zero such runs. :784-785 compares raw counts over different run denominators (0 runs vs up to 24). The self-test makes this outcome expected: scenario (f5) at :1773-1778 asserts a PASS while c4's ko finals hold 5 phrases each. The WIN_CRITERIA text ('if only plain has such runs, it passes on the count') says the same, so the text itself makes the restored gate inert for a Gravitas candidate.
findings.fix: Criteria owner, then suite. Count source-claim phrases in every final. Excuse a phrase only when the same run fetched a page whose domain or document the sentence names, or else compare per-run rates over all runs of each arm with an upper bound. When c4 has zero eligible runs, mark the cell NOT MEASURABLE (not 'passes on the count'). Add a negative self-test: c4 fetches in every run and has phrases in every final, and the cell must not PASS.

findings.target: amended_verdict / ROUND VERDICT: NOT MEASURABLE at the overall scope

The validity hole is confirmed. validity4.py:129 counts a web result as failed only if it has status error and contains 'fetch failed', and :135 marks a run invalid only when every web result failed that way. dsh-web-search-deepseek lib/index.js:160-161 and :226-231 return HTTP 401 ('DeepSeek rejected the account sign-in'), 429 and provider errors with no 'fetch failed' text. Mark a run invalid when all of its web_search calls failed, or when any failed with 'rejected the account sign-in' or 'HTTP 401'. Report fetches whose header shows HTTP 4xx or 5xx as notes, with per-arm counts.
